content:
According to Mark Gurman's latest "Power On" newsletter, Apple is reportedly considering a series of changes to the App Store. The goal? To boost the potential revenue the App Store generates.

It remains unclear what specific changes Apple plans to make to the App Store. Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported that Apple wants to "find ways to increase profit margins and extract more recurring revenue from the platform," with this work being driven primarily by incoming CEO John Ternus and current Services SVP Eddy Cue.

Reportedly, this initiative is one of the reasons long-time Apple executive Phil Schiller left the company last week. After stepping down as SVP of Marketing in 2020, Schiller became an Apple Fellow, with part of his responsibilities including overseeing the App Store. Schiller is not in favour of the idea:

There are many ways Apple could increase App Store profit margins. It could eliminate the human app review process, which in the age of agentic coding may be costly and not particularly effective. Further automating app review, though, is unlikely to be popular with users, but would certainly help cut costs.

Top-rated reviews from SF

Given that Apple has long been one of the most valuable companies in the world, if this is true, it's bad news and entirely unnecessary. This would be a very poor signal from the new CEO. I was hoping that having a hardware specialist run the company would bring us back to an Apple that puts products ahead of services again, but this would be a pointless and greedy move. I hope it's not true.

Apple could raise the developer membership fee, currently $99 per year. Given that many small developers are spending $200 a month on Codex and Claude subscriptions to build apps, one could argue Apple is in a position to raise prices without losing users. The company could also charge large developers subscription fees based on traffic, passing on some infrastructure costs.

Only time will tell what actually ends up happening, but I'm keen to see what form any changes might take.
